# Bobby G. Rice

> Country singer-songwriter with 30 charted Billboard singles, two CMA Award nominations (1973), and the #1 country hit "You Lay So Easy On My Mind." Boscobel, Wisconsin native who has been a fixture in country music for over six decades.

## Quick facts
- Full name: Bobby G. Rice
- Genre: Country music
- Career: 1960s — present (60+ years)
- Birthplace: Boscobel, Wisconsin, USA
- Career highlights: 30 Billboard charted singles; biggest hit "You Lay So Easy On My Mind" reached #1 on the Billboard Country chart; two CMA Award nominations in 1973 (Single of the Year + Best Male Vocalist); recorded on GRT Records
- Still actively performing: yes
- Official website: https://www.bobbygrice.com

## Notable songs
- "You Lay So Easy On My Mind" (1973) — #1 Billboard Country
- "Mainstream of Memories"
- "You Give Me You"
- "You Are What Made Me Love You"

## Frequently asked questions

### What is Bobby G. Rice's biggest hit?
"You Lay So Easy On My Mind" — released in 1973, it reached #1 on the Billboard Country chart and earned him CMA Award nominations.

### When was Bobby G. Rice nominated for the CMA Awards?
1973 — nominated for Single of the Year ("You Lay So Easy On My Mind") and Best Male Vocalist of the Year.

### Where is Bobby G. Rice from?
Boscobel, Wisconsin.

### Is Bobby G. Rice still performing?
Yes. He continues to tour and record.

## Also known as
- Bobby Rice
- Bobby G Rice

## Billboard singles named on the site
- Billboard Top 10: "You Give Me You", "Write Me A Letter", "Freda Comes, Freda Goes"
- Also charted: "Pick Me Up On Your Way Down", "My Special Angel", "Sugar Shack", "Hey Baby", "Mountain Of Love"

## Artists who recorded "You Lay So Easy on My Mind"
Loretta Lynn, Conway Twitty, Roy Orbison, David Houston, Kitty Wells, Jerry Springer, Bill Anderson's Po' Boys Band, Pat Boone and Andy Williams.

## Awards and honors listed on the site
- CMA nominations: Male Vocalist, Single and Album of the Year (1973)
- CMA/CRS New Faces artist (1971)
- ASCAP Awards: "You Lay So Easy on My Mind", "You Give Me You", "The Whole World's Makin' Love Again Tonight", "Make It Feel Like Love Again", "The Softest Touch in Town"
- SESAC Award: "Crystal Chandeliers"
- "What Goes Through Your Mind" featured in the movie "The Wooden Bowl"
- Hometown sign in Boscobel, Wisconsin

## TV and radio appearances
Grand Ole Opry; The Louisiana Hayride; WWVA Wheeling Jamboree; Ernest Tubb Midnite Jamboree; Midwest Country (RFD-TV); Ralph Emery Show and Nashville Now; Music Country USA on NBC (the Dean Martin replacement show); The Bill Anderson TV Show; The Wilburn Brothers TV Show; The Ronnie Prophet TV Show (Toronto, Canada); Cheyenne Country and On Stage (TNN).

## Hit albums
You Lay So Easy on My Mind; Hit After Hit; She Sure Laid The Lonelies on Me; Write Me a Letter; Instant Rice (The Best Of Bobby G. Rice); With Love from Bobby G. Rice.
